class.name: PhysXGas3D
class.brief_description: A sparse-grid Eulerian smoke/gas volume, provided by the PhysX module.
class.description: An early, v1 volumetric gas/smoke solver: a persistent velocity+density field on a block-sparse hash grid, advected with trilinear semi-Lagrangian sampling, driven by [member buoyancy] and real vorticity confinement, and continuously fed from [member source_position]. Runs on plain compute shaders (a private local [RenderingDevice]), not CUDA -- independent of whether the PhysX GPU/CUDA path is available. Unlike [PhysXParticleFluid3D] and [PhysXGranular3D], this is not a particle system -- it shares only its block-hash lookup technique with their block-sparse grid, not their solve. Renders through a stock [FogVolume] + [FogMaterial]: the solver's density grid is baked into an [ImageTexture3D] each step and handed to [member FogMaterial.density_texture], so the actual raymarching, camera-frustum froxel integration, temporal reprojection and light/shadow scattering are all engine code, not anything custom here. [b]FogVolume rendering requires [member Environment.volumetric_fog_enabled] to be on in the scene's active Environment -- this is a hard, scene-wide, all-or-nothing switch (it gates whether the engine's froxel fog buffer exists at all), not something this node can turn on by itself. With it off, this node (and every other [FogVolume] in the scene) draws nothing, silently. A configuration warning is shown in the editor when this is the case; [member volumetric_render] can be turned off in favour of [member debug_point_cloud] if you don't want to enable scene-wide volumetric fog.[/b] [b]v1 scope, worth knowing before relying on this:[/b] [member domain_size]'s world footprint (X/Z and the bottom of Y) is frozen at the node's transform when it first configures and does not follow the node afterward -- a node that moves far from its start loses whatever crosses that boundary. The box's TOP does grow automatically as a plume rises past it (periodically, a few blocks at a time, up to 3x the configured height), so vertical headroom mostly takes care of itself; lateral spread past [member domain_size]'s X/Z does not. There is no pressure projection, so the flow is not divergence-free -- its spread comes from a diffusion term standing in for that, the same technique Stam's stable-fluids method uses for viscosity. Colliders (up to 4, see [member colliders]) are voxelized solids (forced empty and still every step), not a proper no-slip/free-slip boundary.

members.member: World size of the fixed grid box, centered on the node. Rounded up to whole 4-cell blocks per axis. Frozen the first time the solver configures (on entering the tree) -- changing it after that reconfigures (and clears) the grid.
Grid cell size in meters. Also reconfigures the grid when changed.
Local-space position the gas is continuously injected from.
Radius (meters) of the injection region around [member source_position].

Local-space velocity injected into the source region each step, plus a small per-cell random jitter scaled by its magnitude -- a perfectly symmetric source gives vorticity confinement nothing to amplify, so a little injected asymmetry is what seeds any swirl.
Density injected into the source region each step (clamped up to at least this, never down -- the source tops up, it does not overwrite a denser cell).
Upward acceleration applied to a cell's velocity, scaled by its own density. Negative sinks instead of rises (a heavier-than-air gas).

Vorticity confinement strength -- pumps energy back into small eddies the grid's own numerical diffusion would otherwise smear away. Only amplifies curl that already exists (see [member source_velocity]'s jitter); it does not manufacture swirl from nothing.
Per-step density multiplier (how fast the gas fades). [code]1.0[/code] never dissipates; lower values fade faster.

Up to 4 [Node3D] paths; each one's global position drives a sphere obstacle. Every cell inside a sphere is forced empty and still each step, so the field parts and flows around it. A [CollisionShape3D] (or [CollisionObject3D]) carrying a [SphereShape3D] gets its own world-scaled radius from that shape; anything else (a plain [Node3D], or a shape other than a sphere) falls back to [member collider_radius].
Fallback radius (meters) for entries in [member colliders] that are not a sphere-shaped [CollisionShape3D]/[CollisionObject3D]. [code]0[/code] disables such an entry.

Draws the gas through a [FogVolume] + [FogMaterial] (see the class description for the [member Environment.volumetric_fog_enabled] requirement). Turning this off frees the [FogVolume] and its baked texture.

[member FogMaterial.density] on the managed [FogMaterial] -- multiplies the solver's raw density values (roughly [code]0..1[/code]) to a visible opacity. Raise it if the smoke looks too faint, lower it if it looks solid/opaque.
[member FogMaterial.albedo] on the managed [FogMaterial] -- the smoke's scattering colour.

Also (or instead) draws a debug point cloud (a [MultiMesh] of small cubes, one per grid cell above [member render_threshold], colour-ramped by density) -- useful to sanity-check the raw simulation data against the shaded [member volumetric_render] result, or as a fallback when volumetric fog can't be enabled in the scene.
Minimum density for a cell to appear in [member debug_point_cloud]. Has no effect on [member volumetric_render], which draws the continuous density field as-is.
